name: world-three-city-basin
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A wide elevated view across a fictional Andean high-desert basin in 2043. The foreground is a dry, mineral-streaked slope with a massive shared infrastructure spine: a water conduit, energy lines, transit rails, access gates, and control nodes running across the basin. In the middle distance, Keel occupies the highest, harshest terrain around an exhausted open-pit copper or polymetallic hard-rock mine, with tailings, tunnels, pumps, maintenance structures, and repaired industrial housing. Halyard sits on an intermediate industrial plateau, marked by laboratories, fabrication facilities, foundries, greenhouse or vertical-agriculture structures, compute facilities, maker districts, and industrial towers. Oasis lies farther away near a lower salar edge, visibly cleaner and more spacious, with safe infrastructure, comfortable sparse housing, automated transport, and maintained planted areas. The cities are distinct in material condition and social texture but visibly connected by the same physical systems. The route between them should feel like a journey of 80–180 kilometres, taking hours rather than minutes, not a continuous metropolitan sprawl.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Keel must read as the lowest and poorest city tier despite being technologically advanced. Its open pit, legacy mine works, pumps, tailings, and worn industrial systems must be legible. Halyard must read as the industrial and innovation tier, with technical production and research visibly integrated into the city. Oasis must read as the most materially secure tier, with abundant clean water, safe streets, automated services, housing, healthcare infrastructure, and civic systems. The basin must be high, dry, and mineral rather than lush. The shared water conduit, energy lines, transit rails, control nodes, permission gates, and long-distance infrastructure route must visibly connect all three cities.

Not established, so your choice: The exact arrangement of the cities within the basin, the colors and architectural styles of individual buildings, the amount of visible traffic, the number of people, the appearance of the salar, the exact cloud cover, and the details of distant mountain forms are open. The image may show drones, projected interfaces, automated vehicles, and other established systems where they help distinguish the tiers, but their exact designs are free.

Must not appear: Do not depict three unrelated technological eras. Do not make Keel a primitive settlement, Halyard a seamless futuristic megacity, or Oasis a fantasy palace. Do not use real-world landmarks or identify the basin as an actual Atacama or Puna location. Do not show a single centralized skyscraper or visible throne as the source of all authority. Do not make the cities minutes apart or merge them into one urban mass.

The look: Documentary-scale environmental concept art with a high but physically grounded vantage, hard daylight, thin dry air, mineral dust, faded industrial colors, and strong atmospheric distance. The future should appear retrofitted onto older infrastructure: patched conduits, weathered buildings, newer sensors, and clean automated systems sharing the same landscape. Use visual contrast between Keel's oxidized machinery, Halyard's active production, and Oasis's quiet cleanliness without turning any tier into a caricature.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: location-halyard-maker-district
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

A Halyard maker district combining a fabrication workshop, water-technology laboratory, and industrial street. In the foreground, human workers handle modular water-system components: membrane housings, pretreatment equipment, mineral-recovery parts, sensor modules, pipes, and unfinished community water nodes. The components are distributed across several workstations rather than assembled as one monumental machine. Behind them are a foundry, fabrication gantries, greenhouse or vertical-agriculture structures, compute infrastructure, and industrial towers. A Charter House facility is visible nearby, with a controlled registry or access area connecting institutional ownership to the physical workspaces.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Halyard must read as the industrial and innovation tier. Show laboratories, fabrication equipment, foundry-scale production, advanced materials, compute infrastructure, maker districts, and human technical labor in the same frame. The water system must look modular and feedstock-dependent rather than magical: membrane replacement, pretreatment, substantial electrical equipment, trained maintenance, and limited-throughput processing should be visually apparent. Include evidence of many contributors working on related pieces rather than a single inventor's isolated machine.

Not established, so your choice: The exact appearances of the workers, Charter House architecture, registry interface, fabrication tools, greenhouse structure, labels, and workshop organization are open. The image may show a partial purification demonstration or clean output container, but the exact status of the prototype and the composition of the water are free. House colors and emblems may be chosen if they do not establish additional story facts.

Must not appear: Do not depict the water technology as a limitless abundance machine, a single glowing reactor, or a fully autonomous factory. Do not erase human labor. Do not make Halyard uniformly egalitarian or uniformly oppressive; the city contains Charter Houses, workers, partners, cooperatives, independent workshops, and new ventures. Do not add a spaceport or orbital structure unless it is only a distant, non-specific reference to Astra's wider field.

The look: Dense but legible industrial daylight, with a layered view from tactile foreground tools to active fabrication in the middle distance and Halyard's towers behind. Use steel, ceramic, translucent membranes, stained concrete, warm work lights, green plant growth, and cool compute light. The future should feel like advanced equipment installed in an active, crowded workshop whose surfaces are handled and repaired, not a showroom.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: character-alex-phantum
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

Full-body reference portrait of Alex Phantum, age 17, standing in a Keel industrial setting. He is lean and mechanically capable, with a practical, alert posture and a family resemblance to Adrian expressed through the shape of his jaw and a slight thinking head tilt. He wears worn mining or maintenance work clothes and carries a weathered tool bag. One hand turns an old casino chip etched with a looping equation; the other may rest near a tool or on a piece of aging machinery. His expression is skeptical and guarded rather than theatrical. The background should be a simple, softly focused Keel pump hall or repaired industrial passage.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Alex is seventeen, lean, mechanically capable, and dressed in worn mining or work clothes. Include the weathered tool bag and Adrian's worn casino chip with its looping equation. The chip should be small enough to turn unconsciously in one hand. His posture may include crossed arms or a palm placed on machinery, both established habits. His face must not carry an established scar or other invented distinguishing mark. His overall appearance should fit a worker in Keel rather than a wealthy heir, uniformed official, or polished executive.

Not established, so your choice: Alex's exact skin tone, hair color and style, eye color, facial proportions beyond the family resemblance, height, footwear, garment colors, tool-bag construction, and small signs of wear are open. The tool bag's contents are open. The background machinery may vary within Keel's established industrial vocabulary.

Must not appear: Do not make Alex look older than seventeen, physically imposing, aristocratic, spotless, or conventionally heroic. Do not give him scars, tattoos, military armor, luxury clothing, or a visible badge of political office. Do not depict the casino chip as a hologram or make the looping equation into a large glowing emblem. Do not add a permanent override device or command interface to his clothing.

The look: Grounded graphic-novel character reference, three-quarter standing view, neutral industrial light with a cool projected glow and warm reflected metal. Materials should show use: frayed fabric, repaired seams, dust, scuffed boots, worn leather or composite on the tool bag, and a scratched chip surface. Keep the face readable and the silhouette uncomplicated so the character can be matched consistently across pages.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: scene-workshop-choice
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

Inside Adrian's hidden workshop behind the bookshelf in Grandmother Phantum's Keel home, Alex, Ada, and Bi11bot stand around an organized workbench. Alex, in worn work clothes with his tool bag nearby, has one hand near or on an old machine and the other turning Adrian's casino chip. Ada stands beside him in her dark high-collared top, rivet-studded shoulder strap, and moss-green wrap, watching both the people and the equipment. Bi11bot, child-sized and visibly constructed from aged brass, titanium, and ceramic ivory, faces them from the workbench or floor, with his blue and amber lights active. The room contains equations, water-system diagrams, models, prototypes, a physical key, old books, analog gauges, hidden records, and disconnected components. The composition must make the three figures and the physical evidence equally important.

Must be shown, exactly as written: The workshop is concealed behind a bookshelf in a family home in Keel. Include the old book associated with opening the room, an organized workbench, equations, water-system diagrams, models, prototypes, a physical key, and disconnected or offline artifacts. Alex must be visibly seventeen, lean, mechanically capable, and dressed for Keel work; Ada must retain her established hair, freckles, eyes, clothing, and rooted stance; Bi11bot must retain his child-sized aged-brass, titanium, and ceramic-ivory construction, visible repairs, maker's stamps, optical eyes, lens ring, chest key socket, and blue-and-amber lights. The room should contain no seamless networked command center as its only source of information.

Not established, so your choice: The exact arrangement of the workshop, furniture, wall surfaces, lamp design, color of the family home's interior, number of diagrams, prototype shapes, and relative spacing of the three figures are open. The image may include a small projected interface alongside paper, mechanical, and analog records. Any words on diagrams may be abstract or too small to read unless the established terms are needed as visible text.

Must not appear: Do not depict the workshop as a vast laboratory, corporate facility, pristine showroom, or fantasy treasure chamber. Do not show Alex alone, Bi11bot making a decision for the humans, or Ada reduced to a background observer with no access to the work. Do not add a visible Alpha avatar, a permanent override console, or unestablished weapons. Do not make the three safeguards appear as generic glowing gemstones.

The look: Intimate, low-key workshop lighting with warm lamp pools, deep corners, aged wood or repaired shelving, dust, brass, ceramic, paper, and cool machine accents. Use a medium-wide composition with layered sightlines: bookshelf and concealed doorway behind, workbench and artifacts in the middle ground, and the three figures forming a readable triangle in the foreground. The image should feel materially grounded and production-useful, showing how old offline objects coexist with sophisticated engineering.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: character-ada-veyra
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Full-body reference portrait of Ada Veyra, age 20, standing at a Keel overlook with the city and mine dropping away behind her. She has long, wind-tangled copper hair, freckles, and teal-blue eyes. She wears a dark high-collared top, a rivet-studded shoulder strap, and a muted moss-green wrap. Her stance is steady and rooted, with her attention directed toward Keel rather than toward the distant upper route. Her expression is attentive and emotionally precise, not exaggerated. The background should show enough of Keel's pit, repaired industrial housing, and infrastructure to establish where she belongs.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Ada is twenty. Include long wind-tangled copper hair, freckles, teal-blue eyes, the dark high-collared top, rivet-studded shoulder strap, and muted moss-green wrap. Her posture must be steady and rooted. The overlook must be associated with Keel, and the city should be visible below her. No scars or other distinguishing physical marks are established.

Not established, so your choice: Ada's exact skin tone, body type, height, footwear, garment cut, fabric texture, jewelry, tools, and the precise construction of the overlook are open. Her expression may range from thoughtful to mildly challenging. The weather, time of day, and amount of dust or wind are open.

Must not appear: Do not make Ada look fragile, ornamental, aristocratic, or dressed in generic futuristic bodysuit clothing. Do not remove the shoulder strap or wrap. Do not give her weapons, a uniform, a civic office, or an invented technological implant. Do not make the overlook a lush garden or a polished Oasis terrace.

The look: Wind-shaped documentary portrait with dry high-altitude light, muted mineral colors, copper hair catching the light, and Keel's industrial geometry below. The figure should be sharply readable against a broad landscape, with clothing showing practical wear but not the same degree of industrial grime as Alex's work clothes. The image should communicate rootedness through stance and composition rather than through symbolic props.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: location-keel-pump-hall
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

Interior of a Keel pump hall built into and around an exhausted hard-rock mine. The room is large enough for industrial water machinery, with aging pumps, thick pipes, valves, analog gauges, maintenance platforms, access doors, and patched structural supports. Older metalwork bears repeated repairs, replacement plates, welds, mineral deposits, and industrial residue. Newer biometric readers, projected procedures, distributed sensors, and a ceiling-mounted surveillance drone have been fitted onto the old machinery. A narrow maintenance route leads toward deeper legacy tunnels and a sealed section of the mine. The space should show how physical systems can be visibly old while the control layer remains sophisticated.

Must be shown, exactly as written: The setting must be Keel: worn mining and maintenance infrastructure, old copper or polymetallic hard-rock workings, pumps, industrial pipes, legacy tunnels, and connected Alpha-controlled equipment. Include at least one analog gauge beside a newer projected or networked readout, allowing the two systems to appear capable of disagreeing. Include a biometric checkpoint or access gate within the pump hall or at the tunnel entrance. The room should be physically functional, not an abandoned ruin; Keel workers keep this machinery operating long after ideal replacement.

Not established, so your choice: Exact pump design, pipe diameter, wall color, warning colors, floor material, tool storage, worker count, drone design, and projected interface layout are open. The image may include dust, condensation, dampness, oil, mineral scale, or loose repair materials, provided the hall remains readable as an operating facility. The projected procedure may contain generic technical graphics rather than legible text.

Must not appear: Do not depict a pristine laboratory, a medieval mine, or a fully automated facility with no human maintenance. Do not use oil-drilling derricks, lithium evaporation ponds, or unrelated extraction machinery as the defining equipment. Do not make every display agree perfectly with every physical gauge. Do not add a giant central AI avatar or a human operator's command throne.

The look: Close documentary industrial photography translated into graphic-novel concept art. Harsh work lights and cool projected light should strike aged brass, steel, ceramic sensor housings, damp stone, and oxidized surfaces. Keep the palette in iron gray, copper, mineral green, dust brown, and pale blue interface light. Composition should emphasize the scale of the pumps and pipes against a worker-sized passage, making the machinery feel both essential and difficult to replace.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: character-bi11bot
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Full-body reference portrait of Bi11bot, a child-sized mechanical figure standing beside an old workbench in Adrian's hidden workshop. His body is visibly made rather than seamless: aged brass, titanium, and ceramic ivory panels meet at tooled seams, repairs, fasteners, and maker's stamps. Soft-blue and amber light accents appear in the body. His expressive optical eyes face the viewer; one eye contains a small adjustable lens ring. A key socket is visible in the center of his chest. His proportions are compact and child-sized, but his construction is precise and functional.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Bi11bot must be child-sized and constructed from aged brass, titanium, and ceramic ivory. Show visible tooled seams, repairs, and maker's stamps. Include soft-blue and amber light accents, expressive optical eyes, one adjustable lens ring, and the chest key socket that awakens him. He must look like Adrian made him as a physical machine, not like a seamless humanoid android or a projected avatar. The hidden workshop background may contain an organized workbench, equations, water-system diagrams, models, and prototypes.

Not established, so your choice: Exact height within child-sized proportions, body silhouette, number and placement of joints, hand design, feet, panel shapes, stamp marks, eye proportions, light intensity, and workshop clutter are open. The image may show the lens ring turned slightly or the head tilted, both established habits. The spoken name need not appear in the image.

Must not appear: Do not give Bi11bot organic skin, a human face, a smooth black consumer-robot shell, a large industrial chassis, or a floating holographic body. Do not depict him as a threatening combat robot. Do not add weapons, wings, or a permanent command console. Do not make the lights bright enough to turn him into a glowing object with no material surface.

The look: Tactile character-design plate with soft workshop light, warm aged metal, ivory ceramic, blue and amber indicator glow, and close enough detail to inspect seams, repairs, lens hardware, and maker's stamps. Keep the expression observant and dry rather than cute or menacing. The workbench should establish scale: Bi11bot is child-sized, while the surrounding workshop contains full-sized tools, diagrams, and water-system components.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.

name: location-oasis-civic-table
prompt:
A photographic concept reference with NO TEXT ANYWHERE IN THE IMAGE: no place names, captions, labels, signage, logos, numbers, speech balloons or on-screen writing, even where a place is named below - the picture identifies things by how they look, never by a word. Not finished comic art; no panel borders.

An Oasis civic interior opening onto a clean, sparse district. The room contains a long decision table with longtime residents and displaced people seated together, while a transparent or projected Alpha interface displays modeled options and consequences without physically dominating the room. Beyond the glass or open threshold are safe streets, automated transportation, comfortable sparse housing, abundant clean water, planted areas maintained by small drones, and civic-service infrastructure. The architecture should be orderly and materially secure, but the civic room should visibly depend on people being present together rather than on automatic service delivery alone.

Must be shown, exactly as written: Oasis must read as the most materially secure tier: clean water, safe infrastructure, housing, healthcare or service access, automated transportation, sparse comfortable architecture, and well-maintained public space. Include both former refugees or displaced residents and longtime residents at the local decision table. Include Alpha as a projected advisory or modeling system rather than a physical ruler. The setting must allow participation and discussion while retaining the clean, efficient, individualized service environment.

Not established, so your choice: The exact number, ages, clothing, ethnicity, and physical appearance of the residents are open. The decision table's shape, the district's architecture, the drone design, plant species, interface color, and the specific modeled issue are open. The interface may show abstract graphs, route lines, water levels, or allocation diagrams without readable text.

Must not appear: Do not make Oasis visibly impoverished, militarized, overcrowded, or ruined. Do not depict displaced people as segregated from the civic table. Do not show Alpha's interface issuing a final decision, commanding the room, or replacing all human presence. Do not turn Oasis into a palace or a sterile all-white science-fiction city.

The look: Quiet, high-key natural light with clean surfaces, pale mineral tones, glass, concrete, water reflections, and restrained vegetation. Keep the composition spacious but not empty. The automated environment should look comfortable and competent, while the human table introduces varied posture, age, clothing, and visual density. A low camera angle at table height should make participation, not architecture, the image's center of gravity.

Add nothing that tells a story of its own: no invented symbols, emblems, documents or events. Render the description, not an interpretation of it.
